checks.issue: ⚠ A ONE-CHARACTER CONFLICT RUNNING THROUGH THE WHOLE BOOK, AND IT NEEDS JOSH AT THE PAGE. Thai-script Pali marks a consonant cluster with either YAMAKKAN ๎ (U+0E4E) or THANTHAKHAT ์ (U+0E4C), and the two are nearly identical at photograph resolution. The app is currently SPLIT: 84 yamakkan against 1054 thanthakhat, and the split is not random — the earliest pages 2-20 and the forward pass's translated-section work at 193-207 use ๎, and everything else, including all of this backward pass, uses ์. So this very section is inconsistent with itself: page 194 has ส๎วากขาโต and page 225 here has ส์วากขาโต for the same word. NOTHING HAS BEEN CHANGED EITHER WAY. This entry follows the house majority. Magnifying page 224 shows a mark shaped like a small loop with a rising tail, which matches the thanthakhat over ฆ in พระสงฆ์ in the Thai text on 225 — but that is the same 'it looks like a known X' argument the ฬ/พ rule was settled against as circular, so it is offered as evidence and not acted on.

THE SHEET PRINTS NO PAGE NUMBER. It is 224 by position: 223 and 225 both print theirs. Section openers in this book are numberless — 193 does the same for the morning service, and the two DIVIDERS at 247 and 277 are numberless too, though those are blank otherwise and this one is not.

THE MORNING AND EVENING OFFERINGS ARE THE SAME EIGHT UNITS WORD FOR WORD as far as the app can tell; the two are entered as separate chants because the book prints them separately, under their own headings, in their own services.

The page prints the formula ONCE and puts (๓ ครั้ง) beneath it in Thai numerals; page 77 prints the line three times over as three verses. The marker is entered as a verse because a page block cannot anchor inside a chant, and the line is NOT repeated three times in the data — that would be printing something the page does not.
